Integrate the derivative with respect to $x$:
$$y = \int (7 - x^2 - 6x)\,dx = 7x - \frac{1}{3}x^3 - 3x^2 + c$$

Substitute the coordinates of the given point $(3, -10)$ to determine $c$:
$$-10 = 7(3) - \frac{3^3}{3} - 3(3^2) + c = 21 - 9 - 27 + c = -15 + c$$
$$c = -10 + 15 = 5$$
$$y = 7x - \frac{1}{3}x^3 - 3x^2 + 5$$

Group and complete the square for the quadratic terms:
$$7 - x^2 - 6x = 7 - (x^2 + 6x) = 7 - \left[(x + 3)^2 - 9\right]$$
$$= 7 + 9 - (x + 3)^2 = 16 - (x + 3)^2$$
where $a = 16$ and $b = 3$.

Set the gradient expression strictly greater than zero:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} > 0 \implies 16 - (x + 3)^2 > 0 \implies (x + 3)^2 < 16$$

Take square roots across the inequality:
$$-4 < x + 3 < 4$$
$$-7 < x < 1 \quad (\text{or } (-7, 1))$$
